summary: Nancy Hock is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She earned her PhD in 1987 from the University of California, Berkeley, supervised by Joanna Gottfried Williams. She held an attested post at the Asian Art Museum in 1987.

Nancy McCagney works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Chögyam Trungpa, Ninian Smart, Gerald James Larson, William F. Powell, and Andrew Rawlinson, and held an attested post at the University of Delaware in 1997.

Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She has served as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Historical Research and as a Project Fellow at the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies (attested 2011).
Nang Dzé Drubpé Dorjé studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Nanigopal Majumdar (1897–1938) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Superintendent at the Archaeological Survey of India from 1931 and as Superintendent of the Archæological Section at the Indian Museum, Kolkata (attested 1939).
Nantu Shaw is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. Supervised by Sthaneshwar Timalsina, Shaw is attested as a visiting scholar at Stony Brook University in 2026.

Naoji Okuyama (b. 1956) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. After completing doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1980–1985), he held teaching posts there (~1985–1993) before becoming a professor at Koyasan University around 1993.
Naoki Nabeshima is a Buddhist studies scholar who founded Ryukoku University and served there as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies (both attested 2004).

Naoko Nishimura is an Indology and linguistics scholar. She earned her PhD from Tohoku University (1993–2002), where she was supervised by Toshifumi Goto, and later served there as a specialized researcher (attested 2026).

Naomi Appleton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford, was a British Academy Postdoctoral Fellow at Cardiff University, and became Professor and Co-Director at the University of Edinburgh.
Naomi Worth studied at the University of Virginia in the fields of Tibetology and religious studies, later holding an attested post there in 2018.
Naomichi Nakada (b. 1928) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under Ram Chandra Pandeya and doctoral supervisor Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale.

Naoshiro Tsuji (1899–1979) was an Indology and linguistics scholar educated at the University of Tokyo and Oxford. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at the University of Tokyo (1942–1960), professor at Keio University, and director of Toyo Bunko.
Naoya Funahashi (b. 1937) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held posts at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science and Otani University (attested 1981).

Narada Maha Thera (1898–1983) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar educated at St. Benedict's College and University College, Colombo. He served as Superior of Vajiraramaya Temple from circa 1955 to 1983.

Narayan Hemandas Samtani (1924–2013) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned his PhD from the University of Delhi under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale in 1961 and served as Lecturer in Pali at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1971).
Narayana Shastri Khiste was an Indology scholar who served as Librarian at Sarasvati Bhavana Library (attested 1932) and as Principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1950).
Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya (1934–2001) was a scholar of history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology who held posts at the University of Calcutta, attested between 1970 and 1999.

Narendrachandra Bhattacharyya worked in Indology and philosophy, serving as General Editor for the Calcutta Sanskrit Series (attested 1936) and as a Pandit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1943).
Naresh Keerthi is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2018–2021) before becoming an Assistant Professor at Ashoka University in 2021.
